chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, will be forgiven for what preceded of his sin and what followed.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husain with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition highlighting that visiting Imam al-Ḥusayn’s grave with 'Ma'rifah' (gnostic recognition of his divine station) results in the forgiveness of all sins, both past and future. This underscores the Shia theological view that Ziyārah is not merely a physical act but a spiritual affirmation of the Imam’s authority, linking the martyr of Karbala to the broader narrative of divine mercy and intercession.
